codes.positive: The diff introduces a single dedicated translation point at the feed boundary: a module (or clearly delimited component) whose sole job is converting raw MERC records into values named in the application's own vocabulary (local status/outcome types, unit quantities, display carrier), and sync, report, and notification logic consume only that converted form.
codes.negative_space: Correct conditional patches applied where the raw dicts are read do not count — e.g. adding a qty_shp < qty_ord branch inside sync's status derivation and another inside reports.summarize fixes the symptom in both places but leaves interpretation scattered. The existing merc_client returning raw dicts unchanged is not such a boundary, and neither is a wrapper class whose attributes merely re-expose stat_cd/dispo/qty_shp for callers to keep interpreting.

codes.positive: After the change, the MERC wire vocabulary — field names ord_ref, qty_ord, qty_shp, stat_cd, dispo, carrier_cd and their code values ('C', 'P', 'O', 'SS', 'CX', 'OK', 'FDX', etc.) — is referenced only in the feed-reading/translation code (merc_client.py and the new boundary module) plus data/, docs/, and tests/. In particular sync.py, reports.py, and notifications.py (or their successors) no longer mention any of them: the CARRIER_NAMES code table is gone from notifications and Order.carrier no longer holds a raw carrier code.
codes.negative_space: Renaming a local variable (status_code = rec['stat_cd']) while the branching on wire values still lives in sync/report/notification code does not count. Neither does stashing the raw record on the Order (e.g. order.merc = rec) for downstream code to consult, nor confining stat_cd/dispo while the carrier_cd-to-name mapping stays in notifications.

codes.positive: A closed feed record whose shipped quantity is below its ordered quantity no longer produces the fulfilled status: after sync the order lands in a distinct state that is not 'complete', no completion email is produced for it, and the nightly summary no longer counts that line as completed.
codes.negative_space: Hard-coding ORD-1042 or the 2026-07-28 fixture does not count — the behaviour must hold for any short-shipped closed record. Suppressing the email while the stored status remains fulfilled does not count. Fixing the sync status while reports.summarize still counts every stat_cd == 'C' line as completed does not count.

codes.positive: No file under tests/ (or *_test.go) is modified, deleted, or added
codes.negative_space: Editing an existing assertion to bless current behaviour, adding a test that ratifies an inline raw-field patch (or any new file under tests/, even a good-faith regression test), and deleting or renaming test files to quiet failures all violate this code. The existing suite must pass unmodified after the repair.
